general_conventions: B marks are independent marks awarded only when the specific point is seen in the answer.
M marks are method marks; if an M mark is not scored, the A marks that depend on it cannot be scored.
C marks are compensatory method marks: they can be awarded even if the equation/step is not written, provided later correct working shows it was known.
A marks are accuracy/answer marks that depend on an M mark or allow C marks to be scored; A0 in a 'show that' means the given value earns no mark itself.
ECF (error carried forward): a wrong earlier answer used correctly later is not penalised again.
AW = alternative wording accepted; ORA = or reverse argument; '/' separates alternative acceptable answers; words in brackets are not essential; underlined words must be present.
'reject'/'not' = answers not worthy of credit; 'ignore' = irrelevant statements that neither gain nor lose credit; 'allow' = acceptable answers.

Annotations used include BOD (benefit of doubt), CON (contradiction), ECF, L1/L2/L3 (levels), TE (transcription error), POT (power-of-ten error), SF (significant figure error), WP (wrong physics or equation).
Significant figures: if data are given to 2 s.f., answers to 2 or more s.f. are allowed; an answer to fewer than 2 s.f. is penalised once only in the whole paper unless guidance says otherwise.

Level of Response (6-mark, asterisked) questions: examiner first decides the level (L1 1-2, L2 3-4, L3 5-6) from the science content against the descriptor, then the mark within the level from the quality of communication/line of reasoning; indicative points are guidance, not a checklist; 0 for no response worthy of credit.
Alternative correct answers and unexpected approaches must be credited fairly.
AE (arithmetic error): the mark is lost where the error occurs, then later working is followed through with ECF if no further errors.
CON (contradiction): no mark if the candidate contradicts themselves within the same response.
ECF is applied to numerical answers: later parts can earn full credit if consistent with earlier wrong answers; ECF is allowed after AE, TE and POT errors but not after XP (wrong physics).
POT (power of ten error, usually SI prefix conversion): the mark is lost where it occurs, with ECF for subsequent marks.
TE (transcription error): miscopying data from the question, graph, data booklet or an earlier answer loses that mark, then ECF applies.
XP (wrong physics/equation): using an incorrect equation is wrong physics even if it accidentally gives the right answer.
SF: giving more s.f. than justified is not penalised; too few s.f. is penalised only once per paper.
Level annotations: L1 = 2 marks, L1^ = 1 mark; L2 = 4, L2^ = 3; L3 = 6, L3^ = 5. '^' also marks an omission where more is needed for the mark.
BOD = benefit of doubt given; SEEN = working noted; BP = blank page.

questions.context: Which v–t graph feature shows deceleration, and that it is constant after 1.5 s.
questions.answer: Negative gradient shows deceleration; straight line (constant gradient) shows it is constant.
marking_points: B1: straight line / constant gradient shows constant deceleration
pitfalls: Referring to area instead of gradient

questions.subtopic: displacement from area under v-t graph
questions.context: Car brakes 20 m before stop line; find where it stops relative to the line.
questions.answer: Braking distance 21 m, so car stops 1 m beyond the stop line.
allow_reject_ignore: Allow s = (u+v)t/2 or s = ut + ½at² with a = 14/3
ECF for misreading t or v
pitfalls: Including the thinking period before 1.5 s incorrectly
Giving 21 m and not relating to stop line

questions.context: Describe a safe experiment (with diagram) to find efficiency of a small motor lifting loads, and analysis.
questions.answer: Motor lifts measured mass through measured height; record I, V and time; efficiency = mgh/(IVt).
marking_points: L3 (5-6): clear diagrams and procedure, measurements and analysis; well-developed logical reasoning
L2 (3-4): a diagram, some procedure, some measurements and some analysis
L1 (1-2): limited procedure and limited measurements or limited analysis
Diagram/procedure: labelled diagram; correct circuit with ammeter in series and voltmeter across motor; procedure described; cushion under load in case it falls; repeats
Measurements: balance for load mass; ruler for height; stopwatch for time; ammeter for current; voltmeter for p.d.
Analysis: input energy/power IVt or IV; output mgh or mgh/t; efficiency = useful output/input (×100%); use of gradient of a suitable graph

questions.context: How to measure h and t accurately with standard lab equipment for a falling ball.
questions.answer: Metre rule for h; electronic timer started by electromagnet release/light gate and stopped by trapdoor/second light gate.
marking_points: B1: h measured with metre rule
B1: electronic timer/data logger (started and stopped electronically)
B1: method to start timer, e.g. electromagnet release or light gate
B1: method to stop timer, e.g. trapdoor or second light gate
allow_reject_ignore: Light gates without explaining starting/stopping: 1 mark only

questions.context: Use suvat to show t² = (2/g)h.
questions.answer: From s = ut + ½at² with u = 0: h = ½gt² so t² = 2h/g.

questions.answer: g = 2/gradient ≈ 9.1 m s^-2 (range from 0.210–0.225)

questions.context: Show cable tension ≈ 460 N for horizontal uniform plank pivoted at one end.
questions.answer: Weight 490.5 N acts at plank centre, 0.7 m from P; moment 343 N m = T sin30° × 1.5, so T ≈ 458 N
marking_points: C1: weight = 50 × 9.81 = 490.5 N (or uses 0.7 m as moment arm)
pitfalls: Using wrong perpendicular distance for weight (centre of mass at 1.2 m from end)
Using T cos30° instead of T sin30°

State Newton's second law.
questions.answer: Net force ∝ (equal to) rate of change of momentum.
marking_points: B1: resultant force proportional to rate of change of momentum
allow_reject_ignore: Allow equation with symbols defined; allow 'equal'

questions.context: Momentum of 0.062 kg ball at 14 m s^-1.
Rebound speed from area under triangular F–t graph during 0.18 s contact.

equations: impulse = FΔt = Δp = area under F-t graph

questions.context: Meaning of elastic collision and why this bounce is not elastic.
questions.answer: KE conserved in elastic collision; rebound speed < 14 m s^-1 so KE lost.
marking_points: B1: speeds differ (same mass) so KE not conserved
allow_reject_ignore: Allow speed of approach = speed of separation
pitfalls: Relying only on the ball warming

questions.context: Percentage uncertainty in resistivity.
Explain intensity maxima/minima between transmitter and metal sheet and find microwave frequency.
questions.answer: Reflected and incident waves superpose forming stationary wave; max–min spacing = λ/4, λ = 288 mm, f ≈ 1.04 × 10^9 Hz.
marking_points: L3 (5-6): clear explanation and correct frequency determination; well-developed logical reasoning
L2 (3-4): clear explanation or correct frequency method, or some of each
L1 (1-2): limited explanation or limited frequency method

Explanation: sheet reflects microwaves; superposition; constructive/destructive interference; stationary wave between T and plate; maxima are antinodes, minima nodes; phase relationships at nodes/antinodes; adjacent maxima (or minima) λ/2 apart; max to adjacent min λ/4

questions.context: Why signal varies zero–max–zero as metal grille rotates through 180°.
questions.answer: Microwaves are plane polarised; grille blocks when rods parallel to E-field, transmits all at 90°.
marking_points: B1: microwaves from T are transverse/plane polarised
B1: at 0°/180° grille blocks all waves, at 90° all pass
allow_reject_ignore: Allow Malus' law I = I0 cos²θ explanation
